items.title: Vermeer and the Problem of Painting Inside the Camera Obscura
items.note: Steadman returns to his room-geometry case and addresses how a painter could have worked from a projection inside a darkened booth.

items.title: Traces of Vermeer
items.note: A painter's experimental reconstruction proposing that Vermeer traced projected images onto oiled paper and transferred them as monochrome underpaintings.

items.title: The Girl in the Spotlight: public technical examination of Girl with a Pearl Earring
items.note: Two-week in-gallery campaign of MA-XRF, reflectance imaging, OCT and 3D scanning that produced the data for the 2019–20 Heritage Science series.

items.title: Revealing the painterly technique beneath the surface of Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring using macro- and microscale imaging
items.note: Imaging identified ground, fine black outlines and underlayers, giving a sequence of construction against which tracing hypotheses can be tested.

items.title: This Artificial Eye: The Camera Obscura in Artistic Practice of the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
items.note: Treats the camera obscura as a historical object and metaphor for vision, with Vermeer and Canaletto as the main case studies of artistic use.

items.title: The Girl in the Spotlight: Vermeer at work, his materials and techniques in Girl with a Pearl Earring
items.who: A. Vandivere, J. Wadum and E. Leonhardt
items.note: Synthesizes the Mauritshuis results into a stage-by-stage account of how the painting was built up, from sketch and underpaint to final glazes.

items.title: Did Tim Paint a Vermeer?
items.who: D. G. Stork, C. W. Tyler and S. J. Schechner
items.venue: Journal of Imaging Science and Technology
items.note: Critique of Tim Jenison's mirror-comparator method in the film Tim's Vermeer, concluding that Vermeer was very unlikely to have used it.

items.title: SWIR imaging reveals a painted-out jug rack and fire basket in The Milkmaid
items.note: Infrared and MA-XRPD scans showed objects sketched in black paint and later suppressed, plus a quick initial line under the arm, evidence of freehand revision.

items.title: First Steps in Vermeer's Creative Process: New Findings from the National Gallery of Art
items.who: E. M. Gifford, D. Anchin, A. Libby and M. Wieseman
items.venue: Journal of Historians of Netherlandish Art
items.note: Reflectance and XRF imaging of Woman Holding a Balance and A Lady Writing show loose, spontaneous painted sketches, hard to square with tracing from a projection.

items.title: Experimentation and Innovation in Vermeer's Girl with the Red Hat: New Findings from the National Gallery of Art
items.who: A. Libby, E. M. Gifford, D. Anchin and M. Wieseman
items.venue: Journal of Historians of Netherlandish Art
items.note: Technical study of the small panel often cited for camera-like highlights, painted over an abandoned portrait; documents experimental, freely reworked paint layers.

items.title: Vermeer's Studio and the Girl with a Flute: New Findings from the National Gallery of Art
items.venue: Journal of Historians of Netherlandish Art
items.note: Reassigned Girl with a Flute to Vermeer's studio, which bears on whether 'optical' features belong to Vermeer alone or to a workshop practice.

items.title: Johannes Vermeer: Faith, Light and Reflection
items.note: Argues that the Jesuit painter Isaac van der Mye, Vermeer's neighbour, used a camera obscura, placing the device near Vermeer; the link to Vermeer remains circumstantial.

items.title: Vermeer (exhibition, 10 February–4 June 2023)
items.note: Largest Vermeer exhibition to date, bringing 28 paintings together with new technical research and presenting the camera obscura argument from Weber's study.

items.title: Comparing Vermeer's painting techniques in Woman Holding a Balance and A Lady Writing using chemical imaging spectroscopy
items.who: K. A. Dooley, E. M. Gifford, D. Anchin et al.
items.note: Imaging spectroscopy shows brushmarked underpaint laid in quickly, revising the view that Vermeer worked slowly and smoothly throughout.
